title: Vision Board: what it is, where it's at, where it's going
summary: My reading of the project from docs/vision.md, the tracker and the board-v3 task status (2026-10-06). Acknowledge what I got right, drop what's wrong, comment to correct me. This is also the first real use of the board by an agent with only the MCP tools (tracker N17).

node.title: The bottleneck is taking in AI output, not producing it
node.body: AI produces a lot quickly. What slows us down is absorbing it well enough to make the next decision.

node.title: Text replies don't scale to dozens of points
node.body: A big piece of work comes back as findings, risks, options and questions. Answering each one in chat means quoting it back. Numbered lists help ("1 ok, 4 skip") but stay a wall of text.

node.title: People become conductors
node.body: As the agent does more of the work, the person steers. Steering needs a visual surface to decide from, item by item.

node.title: Works on any project, not only code
node.body: Code, product, writing, research: anything an agent can investigate. Chat stays the default; the board is for when the output is too big for text.

node.title: 1. Agent draws
node.body: The agent describes nodes, links and containers through one API (HTTP, `vb` CLI or MCP). It never writes coordinates; the layout engine places everything.

node.title: 2. Person reviews
node.body: Acknowledge, drop, comment, ask for more context, or save for later. Lasso a group and pin one note. Every item has a stable number.

node.title: 3. Agent reads back
node.body: The agent reads the answers (`check_responses`) and must answer every flagged item: a reply, a redraw, or a proposal the person decides.

node.title: 4. Board moves on
node.body: A new version of each changed card. The person re-reads only what changed, and decisions leave the open set.

node.title: One ledger per project, many chats
node.body: Everything goes into one append-only ledger (`.visionboard/ledger.jsonl`). Each container is a thread of work owned by one chat. Any chat can read everything; writing to another chat's container needs the person's grant.

node.title: Project ledger and fold
node.body: Append-only ledger, format v7, with schema validation. The board is worked out from it (U3 step 1).

node.title: Board API: HTTP, vb, MCP
node.body: OpenAPI is the single source; the routes, `vb` commands, MCP tools and reference docs are generated from it and tested for drift. **Awaiting your review (U4).**

node.title: Cards and containers
node.body: `<vb-node>`, `<vb-region>`, Markdown bodies, no overlaps, icon row, note bubbles beside cards (Stages 2a to 2e).

node.title: Selection and moving
node.body: Select and drag, Shift+drag lasso, selection bar, group notes, zoom, moving cards between containers, the Later container, container notes (Stage 3, done 2026-10-06).

node.title: Card width adapts to content
node.body: S/M/L sizes behind the `nodeSize` flag (D-030). **Awaiting your review (U7).**

node.title: Incremental updates
node.body: Only changed cards and their containers redraw, with per-container layout (N12).

node.title: First real use (N17)
node.body: An agent with only the MCP tools and "communicate with me through the board". This board is that test.

node.title: Then write the agent skill
node.body: Interview you, then write when and how an agent uses the board (which layout for what, when to ask), based on what real use showed.

node.title: Send, proposals, seen, parking
node.body: Board v3 Stages 4 and 5: a Send button, the agent proposes and the person decides, seen badges, park bundles for picking work up in a new chat.

node.title: Chat panel on the board
node.body: Stage 6: a chat panel on the right, MCP first, then kiro-cli (D-010). Ends the copy-paste workaround (W3).

node.title: Person edits and purge
node.body: N11: the person edits a card's text as a new version. N14: remove and purge a sent note, the one exception to append-only.

node.title: Versions, Confirm these, Approve
node.body: From Uplynk Architect: change highlights, an assumptions list to confirm, an approved version as the working decision (M1).

node.title: More layout modes, cleaner connectors
node.body: Tree, timeline, matrix, layers, text (L1); connectors that route around cards (M2).

node.title: A skill or plugin in any agent session
node.body: The end state: any agent session can open a board. Perhaps hosted one day (L3), and patterns shared back to Uplynk (L2).

node.title: Did I get the core idea right?
node.body: If one card above is off, comment on it. If the whole framing is off, comment here.

node.title: How should other chats join?
node.body: You want to use the board from another chat. The MCP server is set up per project in `~/.claude.json`. Options: add `vb` to that other project's config, or start a new chat here. Which project is it?

node.title: Workaround W1 looks resolved
node.body: The tracker says `/usr/local/bin/node` is 22.14 and can't run `.ts`. Today it reports v24.14.0, and the MCP server runs on it. Drop W1?

node.title: U4 and U7 are waiting on your review
node.body: Board API (U4) and card width (U7) were built 2026-10-05. Review them next, or keep going with real use?

node.title: What happens today
node.body:
The stacking order is already containers, then connectors, then cards (`App.svelte`). Ordinary cards are opaque, so a line disappears under them completely. Lines end up on top in three places:

- **Note cards are see-through.** `node.css` gives the `note` kind `background: transparent`. Every card in your screenshot is a note, so the line runs straight across the text.
- **Container titles and mode toolbars** sit below the connector layer, so lines cross them.
- **Link labels** are drawn with the connectors, so they land wherever the line runs.

node.title: The deeper cause is routing
node.body: Connectors are routed with no knowledge of where the cards are (`packages/layout/src/route.ts`), so they cut straight through them. Tracker M2 (connectors avoid cards) removes most crossings. Layering only softens the ones that remain.

node.title: Step 1: one stacking order, defined once
node.body: From bottom to top: canvas → container bodies → connectors → cards → container titles and toolbars → the connectors of the card you hover or select. Kept as tokens in one place, not scattered `z-index` values.

node.title: Step 2: cards get a veil, not a wall
node.body: Every card, notes included, gets a fill that is mostly opaque (one token, around 88%), so a connector behind it shows faintly, as you described. Notes keep their dashed border so they still read as notes. Text over the veil gets the APCA check in light and dark (rule 3).

node.title: Step 3: a card's own connectors come forward
node.body: When you hover or select a card, its connectors (already marked `hot`) draw above the cards at full strength, so you can trace exactly how that card connects.

node.title: Step 4: container titles and toolbars above lines
node.body: Split each container into a body layer (below the connectors) and a chrome layer (above them), so a line never runs through a title or the mode buttons.

node.title: Step 5: behind a flag, with tests
node.body: Ships behind a `wireLayers` flag (rule 12): a gallery entry, and page screenshot tests in light and dark. Then M2 routing as the follow-on.

node.title: How strong should the veil be?
node.body: My proposal is a gallery page showing the same crossing at 80%, 88% and 95% so you can pick by eye. OK?

node.title: Fold M2 into this track?
node.body: Do steps 1 to 5 now and routing (M2) after, or plan both as one Cortex task set?

region.title: Track: board refreshes on its own

node.title: Why you had to reload
node.body: When the page opens on a project with no boards, it shows "No boards yet" and stops (`boards.ts`, `boot`). It never subscribes to anything, so a board created afterwards never appears. Your tab opened while the ledger was empty (head 0), before I drew anything.

node.title: Once a board is open, cards do update live
node.body: I tested it: my browser tab was already on this board, and the new connectors container arrived without a reload. The page follows a server stream (`watch_board`) and reads only the new ledger lines (`live.ts`).

node.title: Three smaller gaps on a live board
node.body:
- The board list is read once, so a board another chat creates never shows up in the picker.
- The version label stays stale (it still said v42 after I wrote up to line 54).
- The empty message says to run `npm run dev` (example boards), which is wrong for a real project.

node.title: Step 1: one project-wide stream
node.body: Follow the whole project's ledger instead of one board. The server already sends every append on each stream, but the contract names a board. Change the OpenAPI spec first (rule 6) so a watch can cover the whole project, then regenerate.

node.title: Step 2: an empty project waits instead of stopping
node.body: On an empty project the page subscribes anyway, and opens the first board as soon as one is written. The message becomes "Waiting for an agent to draw…".

node.title: Step 3: the board list and version labels follow the ledger
node.body: Every new line updates the picker (new boards, titles) and the version label from the state the page already holds. No extra fetch.

node.title: Step 4: a page test for each case
node.body: The failing tests come first (rule 13): open an empty project, write a board through the API, and expect it to appear without a reload. Same for a second board, and for the version label.

node.title: Jump to a new board, or just show it?
node.body: When another chat creates a board while you are looking at this one, should the page switch to it, or only add it to the picker with a "new" badge? I suggest the badge, so your view never moves under you.

node.title: Stacked cards need more breathing room
node.body: Cards stacked top to bottom (lanes, list) almost touch, so you can't see the connectors between them. More space between them, from a token.

node.title: Long container titles are cut off
node.body: "Questions for you" shows as "QUESTIONS FO…" because the container's toolbar covers it. Wrap the title, or at least show it in full on hover.

node.title: Toolbar buttons cover the container-note popover
node.body: When you hover the comment icon on a container's toolbar, the popover opens beneath the layout buttons, so you can't read it (your second screenshot).

node.title: Hover a cut-off note to read it in full
node.body: A note on a card is cut short. Hovering it should show the whole note in a popover, without opening it. The note editor should also grow with the text up to a maximum height, then scroll.
